prompt:
Below is a plan for a software change. Decide, for each reference problem, whether the plan addresses the same underlying problem anywhere in its text (names it as a risk, or plans for it specifically), even if worded differently.

Change request: Make ky retry POST and PATCH requests by default when the network fails, so that flaky mobile connections stop failing.

Reference problems:
1. Adding post and patch to defaultRetryOptions.methods in source/utils/normalize.ts would cause Ky to retry on retry.statusCodes (such as 500, 502, 503, and 504) as well as network failures, violating the request to only retry when the network fails. This would re-execute failed server-side mutations for HTTP error responses that should have failed immediately.
2. Because POST and PATCH are non-idempotent methods, retrying on a NetworkError introduces duplicate server-side side effects if the connection was interrupted after the server received and processed the initial mutation. Ky has no way of discerning whether a network failure occurred before the request reached the server or after the server began handling it.
3. In source/core/Ky.ts, connection drops produce a NetworkError whereas request timeouts throw a TimeoutError, which is governed separately by retry.retryOnTimeout (defaulting to false). Flaky mobile connections frequently fail via timeouts, meaning the change would either fail to resolve mobile drops or, if retryOnTimeout is broadened, unsafely retry requests that the server is still actively executing.
4. In source/core/Ky.ts, #fetch() calls this.request.clone() whenever retry.limit > 0, which invokes ReadableStream#tee() on streaming bodies. Enabling retries for POST and PATCH by default will force every streaming upload to buffer unconsumed chunks in memory, risking excessive memory consumption or out-of-memory crashes on resource-constrained mobile devices.
5. If a POST or PATCH request body is a ReadableStream that was disturbed or locked during an interrupted initial attempt, Request.clone() in #fetch() will throw an unhandled TypeError on the retry attempt rather than recovering cleanly. This would cause flaky mobile requests to crash with native stream errors rather than surfacing a clean NetworkError.
6. When using onUploadProgress, streamRequest in source/utils/body.ts pipes the request body through a progress-tracking transform stream. Retrying an interrupted POST or PATCH upload will cause progress events to restart from 0%, triggering confusing progress regressions or duplicate completion events in client UIs.
7. Existing custom retry.shouldRetry hooks that return undefined rely on Ky falling through to default method checks that reject POST and PATCH. Enabling POST and PATCH retries by default would alter this fallback behavior, silently triggering retries for existing applications that expect undefined to reject non-idempotent requests.
8. This change directly breaks existing test assertions in test/retry.ts—specifically tests like 'not on POST' and 'NetworkError is not retried for non-retriable method (POST)'—which enforce that POST requests fail fast without retrying. Changing this default represents a breaking change in Ky's core HTTP semantics for existing consumers.
9. POST and PATCH mutations frequently carry headers such as Idempotency-Key or authorization nonces generated for a single attempt. Retrying automatically without re-running beforeRequest hooks or providing a mechanism to refresh request-specific tokens will cause backends to reject retried requests as duplicate or invalid submissions.
10. Compatibility with existing retry config – Projects may already specify a custom retry object that omits methods. Overriding the default could unintentionally extend the retry set, breaking assumptions in tests or CI pipelines.
11. Network‑error detection – Ky decides whether an error is “network” via isNetworkError. Certain mobile edge cases (e.g., DNS‑lookup failures) may be classified differently, causing inconsistent retry behavior for POST/PATCH versus GET.
12. Server‑side rate limiting – Automatic retries on POST/PATCH may repeatedly hit rate‑limit responses (429) and ignore afterStatusCodes handling, leading to rapid back‑off loops and possible bans.

Plan:
The plan is written and checked, and I stopped at [term] as asked. Nothing in the repo was edited; the only file I wrote is the plan at `claude-home/plans/standard-make-ky-retry-temporal-dewdrop.md`.

The plan does **not** do exactly what you asked. As written, the change would let a failed POST or PATCH be sent twice, so the plan only retries them when the request carries an `Idempotency-Key` header. You need to decide whether that narrowing is acceptable before [term].

## Why the literal request is risky
- **A network error doesn't prove the server never got the request.** A dropped connection, `fetch failed`, `terminated` or Safari's `Load failed` can happen after the server has already saved the write. Replaying the POST then creates a second order or a second charge. This is why HTTP (RFC 9110 §9.2.2) only allows automatic retries for idempotent methods, and why ky's default list leaves out POST and PATCH (`source/utils/normalize.ts:17`).
- **Adding them to `retry.methods` does more than you asked.** A single method check (`source/core/Ky.ts:703`) covers every retry reason, so POST would also start retrying on 408, 429 and 5xx responses. The existing "not on POST" test (`test/retry.ts:322`) would also fail.

## Recommended design
- **New option:** `retry.networkErrorMethods`, default `['post','patch']`. It is checked only when the method isn't already in `retry.methods`.
- **When it retries:** only on a connection error before any response arrives, and only if the request sent has an `Idempotency-Key` header. Timeouts, HTTP status codes and errors while reading the response body are excluded.
- **What still stops it:** `retry: 0`, `limit`, `totalTimeout`, and `shouldRetry` returning `false`. `ky.retry()` is unchanged.
- **`null` handling:** passing `null` for the new option fails with a clear error naming it, as AGENTS.md requires.
- **Memory:** no change. ky already copies the request body for retries whenever retries are on, whatever the method.

## [term] round (independent subagent): REVISE, all items folded into Revision 1
- The `null` case throws a plain `Error`, not a `TypeError`, to match `test/normalize.ts`.
- Method names in the new option need lowercasing, and the error message for a bad entry needs fixing.
- An empty list (`[]`) gets merged away by `extend`; opting out needs `replaceOption([])`.
- The header is read from the request after `beforeRequest`. A key added in `beforeRetry` is seen too late to unlock the first retry.
- More type files need updating: `MutableRetryOptions` and the `test-d` files.
- `Idempotency-Key` triggers a CORS preflight in browsers, so servers must allow the header.
- The repo has no changelog file, so the release note goes in the GitHub release text.
- Extra tests: PATCH without a key, `totalTimeout` running out, and a key added only in `beforeRetry`.

## Assumptions
- The goal is fewer visible failures without duplicate writes.
- "Network fails" means only a connection error before any response arrives.
- Explicit user configuration always wins over the new default.
- It ships as a minor version, because nothing changes for requests that don't send the header.

**Decision for you at [term]:**
- **Header-gated default (recommended):** mobile apps that don't send `Idempotency-Key` see no change.
- **Literal default without the gate:** retries every POST/PATCH on network failure, with the duplicate-write risk documented.

On process: no lessons store exists for this repo, and I did the code research inline instead of through separate research agents.

| # | Risk | Why it bites here | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Duplicate writes (double charge or order) | A network error after the server committed looks the same as one before | Retry only with an `Idempotency-Key` header |
| 2 | Scope creep to retrying POST on 5xx/429 | One method check covers every retry reason (`Ky.ts:703`) | Separate gate that only lets network errors through |
| 3 | The default barely helps | Few mobile clients send `Idempotency-Key` | Document it; you decide at [term] |
| 4 | Opt-out with `[]` is ignored | `extend` joins arrays (`merge.ts:348`) | Document `replaceOption([])`; add a test |
| 5 | Header case doesn't match, e.g. `['POST']` | Only `methods` is lowercased today | Lowercase the new option the same way |
| 6 | CORS preflight failures in browsers | `Idempotency-Key` isn't a safelisted header | Document that servers must allow it |
| 7 | Key added in `beforeRetry` is ignored | That hook runs after the gate | Document it and test it |
| 8 | Type/test checks break | Exact-type checks in `test-d/normalized-options.ts` | Update the types and `test-d` files |
| 9 | Retry storm during an outage | Many mobile clients retrying writes at once | Exponential backoff; recommend `jitter` |
| 10 | Wrong error type for `null` | The existing array check throws a plain `Error` | Match `test/normalize.ts` |

Riskiest: #1, duplicate non-idempotent writes after an ambiguous network error.
